list: Balances and movements for chosen accounts and customers or suppliers
Every posting by account, with running balance
Customer and vendor receivables and payables by age: 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ days
All journal entries in a period, with debit and credit lines
Postings grouped by project, with totals
Locate Journal Transaction by Amount Range
Find entries between two amounts in AED
Locate Journal Transaction by FC Amount Range
Find entries between two amounts in a foreign currency, e.g. USD or CNY
Entries that came from journal vouchers
Postings listed by source document: invoices, payments, deliveries
VAT reports: tax report, reconciliation, VAT return boxes
Open invoices and credit notes for each customer
frepacc.note: Every report can be filtered by branch, cost centre and date, and exported to Excel or PDF. Ask AI in plain words, e.g. “show entries over 50,000 AED last month”, and it opens the right report with the filters set.

list: Product families with their own accounts and costing, e.g. Packaging, Finished goods, Raw materials, Spare parts
Up to 64 yes/no tags per item, e.g. Fragile, Own brand, Needs artwork, Food contact
Dubai main warehouse, quarantine, goods in transit from China, factory stock at suppliers
PCS, CTN, BOX, KG, CBM, ROLL
Conversions per item, e.g. 1 CTN = 24 PCS, 1 PALLET = 40 CTN
Units for item and carton dimensions: mm, cm, m
Units for weight: g, kg, ton
HS codes and customs duty rate per group for UAE imports
Factories and brands that make your items, linked to China suppliers
Sea FCL, sea LCL, air freight, courier, local truck
Physical sites: Dubai, Shenzhen, Foshan, Dongguan, Ningbo
How often stock is counted: daily, weekly, monthly
Which items or warehouses are counted on which cycle, e.g. fast movers weekly
Carton, pallet, bag, crate — used in Pick and Pack and packing lists
Shelves and bins inside each warehouse — rows, racks, levels, bin codes
setupinv.note: Units of Measure Groups and Package Types feed the packing list and container plan for China shipments. AI suggests which items to count each cycle from stock differences and movement.

list: Bank list with SWIFT/BIC codes — UAE banks and the Chinese banks your suppliers use
Your own accounts: AED current account, USD account for China payments, IBAN and G/L account for each
Card types you accept or use, e.g. Visa, Mastercard, company cards
When card payments are settled to the bank, e.g. 2 days after the sale
Pay in full or in instalments, per card type
Card acquirers and payment providers, with their fee per transaction
Who pays bank charges on transfers: OUR, SHA or BEN
Bank transfer, cheque, cash, telegraphic transfer (TT) for China, used by the Payment Wizard
setupbank.note: House Bank Accounts link to your bank statements, so AI can match each statement line to a payment or receipt automatically. Payments to China suppliers default to TT from the USD account.

list: Country list with ISO codes — UAE, China, Oman, KSA, India and others
How addresses print per country, e.g. UAE: building, street, area, emirate, P.O. Box
Retail chains, distributors, wholesale, e-commerce, export
China factories, local suppliers, freight forwarders, service providers
Up to 64 yes/no tags, e.g. Key account, Needs PI before order, Own brand
Priority levels used when stock is short — who gets served first
Reminder stages for overdue invoices: friendly reminder, second notice, final notice
When each reminder is sent, interest and fees, which levels apply
Cash, Net 30, Net 60, 30% advance + 70% before shipment, credit limits
Reasons to stop paying a supplier invoice, e.g. Quality claim, Missing documents
Customer lists for campaigns, e.g. Hypermarkets UAE, GCC distributors
Groups for sending documents and reminders, e.g. Accounts team, Purchasing
setupbp.note: Payment Terms carry your China supplier terms (advance before shipment) and customer credit limits. AI uses Dunning Levels to draft reminders for overdue invoices and asks before sending.

list: Accounts, sign-in, branch, active or inactive
Group users by role to give the same rights at once
Default branch, warehouse, price list and print layout per user
Salespeople in Dubai and buyers in the China offices
Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Northern Emirates, GCC export
Commission rates by group of salespeople
Standard terms and notes for documents, in English, Arabic and Chinese
English, Arabic and Chinese for documents and screens
Link outside numbers (customer PO, factory PI) to documents
Freight and extra charge types added to documents
Which alerts each user gets — in app, email or WhatsApp
Print layouts for every document, with a visual editor
Default Elements for SAP Crystal Reports

Print straight to office and warehouse printers

In Southfield: built-in report engine, nothing to set up

In Southfield: analytics models on your Supabase database
setupgen.note: Crystal Reports, Crystal Server, SAP Links and HANA models are SAP technology. Southfield runs on Supabase with its own report engine, so these 4 become simpler built-in settings — your layouts and reports are rebuilt during migration.

list: Add, move or rename accounts — same screen as Financials › Edit Chart of Accounts

AED, USD, CNY, EUR, SAR — rounding and decimals

Track income and cost per project across all documents

Lines of the cash flow statement and what feeds them

acct.title: Account determination
acct.sub: Which G/L accounts each kind of asset posts to: the asset itself, its yearly depreciation, and the depreciation built up so far.
acct.note: Before the first depreciation run, AI checks that every asset class points to a complete set of accounts.

types.title: Depreciation types
types.sub: How an asset loses value over time. Each asset class uses one type.
types.note: Straight line is the usual choice. Moulds use Manual so their value can follow the number of shots they have done.

areas.title: Depreciation areas
areas.sub: Parallel sets of books for the same asset. Only areas that post to the G/L change your accounts.
areas.note: UAE corporate tax usually follows your book depreciation, so the Tax area stays off unless your accountant asks for it.
rows: Only if tax depreciation differs from book

classes.title: Asset classes
classes.sub: Groups of similar assets. A new asset takes its depreciation and accounts from its class.
classes.note: When you create an asset from an A/P invoice, AI suggests the class from the item and supplier.

attr.title: Attribute groups
attr.sub: Extra fields an asset class needs that are not on the standard asset card.
attr.note: For moulds, AI warns when shots done get close to the mould’s rated life, or when a mould sits at a factory with no production orders.

acct.title: Account determination
acct.sub: Which G/L accounts each kind of asset posts to: the asset itself, its yearly depreciation, and the depreciation built up so far.
acct.note: Before the first depreciation run, AI checks that every asset class points to a complete set of accounts.

types.title: Depreciation types
types.sub: How an asset loses value over time. Each asset class uses one type.
types.note: Straight line is the usual choice. Moulds use Manual so their value can follow the number of shots they have done.

areas.title: Depreciation areas
areas.sub: Parallel sets of books for the same asset. Only areas that post to the G/L change your accounts.
areas.note: UAE corporate tax usually follows your book depreciation, so the Tax area stays off unless your accountant asks for it.
rows: Only if tax depreciation differs from book

classes.title: Asset classes
classes.sub: Groups of similar assets. A new asset takes its depreciation and accounts from its class.
classes.note: When you create an asset from an A/P invoice, AI suggests the class from the item and supplier.

attr.title: Attribute groups
attr.sub: Extra fields an asset class needs that are not on the standard asset card.
attr.note: For moulds, AI warns when shots done get close to the mould’s rated life, or when a mould sits at a factory with no production orders.

count.title: Inventory counting
count.sub: Count sheets by warehouse and area. Staff count on their phone by scanning bins and items.
count.note: Staff do not see the system quantity while counting, so the count is honest. Bins come from Bin Locations.

post.title: Inventory posting
post.sub: Post the counted quantities and book the differences to the stock variance account.
post.note: Aisle C is short by AED 12,400 in total. Differences above AED 5,000 need approval, and AI suggests recounting the baking mats before posting.

mgmt.title: Batch management
mgmt.sub: Assign, split or change batches on goods receipts, deliveries and returns — and lock a batch for QC.
mgmt.note: AI warns 90 days before a batch expires and picks the batch that expires first when goods are delivered.

det.title: Batch details
det.sub: Everything about one batch: supplier, received date, QC result, and every customer it went to.
det.note: If a customer complains, open the batch to see every customer who received it — a recall list in one click.
rows: On QC hold — 1,200 PCS in zone Q

mgmt.title: Serial number management
mgmt.sub: Assign, complete or change serial numbers on goods receipts, deliveries and returns.
mgmt.note: On goods receipt from China, AI reads the serial numbers from the supplier’s packing list so staff do not type them one by one.

det.title: Serial number details
det.sub: The full life of one serial number: received, moved, sold, returned, under warranty.
det.note: Scan or type a serial number to see its whole history. Service calls open this view to check warranty.
rows: Received 2 Sep · sold 12 Oct · Al Noor Trading LLC
Sold 3 Aug · returned 20 Oct · faulty motor

due.title: Internal reconciliation by due date
due.sub: Reconciliations listed by the due date of the invoices they closed.
due.note: Click a reconciliation to open it in Financials › Internal Reconciliations, where it can be viewed or cancelled.

amt.title: Internal reconciliation by exact amount
amt.sub: Open items where an invoice and a payment have exactly the same amount.
amt.note: AI lists exact-amount pairs that are still open and suggests reconciling them; you confirm each one.

trx.title: Internal reconciliation by transaction number
trx.sub: Each journal transaction and the reconciliation it belongs to.
trx.note: Transactions not yet reconciled are highlighted so finance can close them before month-end.

bud.title: Budget report
bud.sub: Budget against actual for each account and cost centre — Main scenario, Jul–Sep 2026.
bud.note: Freight in is 11% over budget. AI traces it to the September containers from Ningbo and shows the invoices behind it.

bs.title: Balance sheet budget report
bs.sub: Planned balance sheet against actual on 30 Sep 2026.
bs.note: Inventory is AED 920,000 above plan — cash is tied up in stock. Check slow movers in Inventory Reports.

tb.title: Trial balance budget report
tb.sub: Every account with its budget and actual for Jul–Sep 2026.
tb.note: Accounts above 100% are highlighted. Budgets come from Financials › Budget Setup.

pl.title: Profit and loss statement budget report
pl.sub: Planned profit and loss against actual for Jul–Sep 2026.
pl.note: Net profit is AED 220,000 below budget: revenue 220,000 short and cost of sales 30,000 over, offset by 30,000 lower operating expenses.

bs.title: Balance sheet comparison
bs.sub: Two dates side by side — here 30 Sep 2026 against 30 Sep 2025. You can also compare branches or companies.
bs.note: AI explains the biggest changes in plain words, e.g. inventory up 22% because three containers from Ningbo arrived in September.

tb.title: Trial balance comparison
tb.sub: Every account for two periods side by side — here Jul–Sep 2026 against Jul–Sep 2025.
tb.note: Pick any two periods, branches or companies. Changes above 15% are highlighted so you can check them first.

pl.title: Profit and loss statement comparison
pl.sub: Income and expenses for two periods side by side — here Jul–Sep 2026 against Jul–Sep 2025.
pl.note: Cost of sales grew faster than revenue (16% against 12%), so gross margin fell from 30.1% to 28.0%. AI points to higher freight-in from China as the main cause.

tax.title: Tax report
tax.sub: Taxable amounts and VAT for the quarter, by tax group. Sample quarter: Jul–Sep 2026.
tax.note: Click a tax group to see every invoice behind it. AI flags invoices to UAE customers that were posted as zero rated.

eu.title: EU sales report
eu.sub: Report of sales to VAT-registered customers in EU countries.
eu.note: This is an EU VAT report. Your company files UAE VAT, so it stays switched off. Exports to Europe still appear in the Tax Report as zero rated.
rows: No EU VAT registration — kept to match SAP

wht.title: Withholding tax report
wht.sub: Tax held back from supplier payments, by withholding code.
wht.note: Withholding tax is switched off (see Setup › Financials › Tax), so this report is empty unless an office outside the UAE needs it.

rec.title: Tax reconciliation report
rec.sub: Compares the VAT accounts in the general ledger with the tax report.
rec.note: AI finds the documents behind any difference — usually a journal entry posted straight to a VAT account. Here: JE 4471 on 28 Sep, AED 1,150.

box.title: Tax declaration box report
box.sub: Your UAE VAT return (VAT 201), box by box, filled from the tax groups.
box.note: Net VAT due for the quarter: AED 134,000 (560,000 payable − 426,000 recoverable). AI prepares the return from these boxes; you review it and submit it to the FTA.

cust.title: Customer receivables aging
cust.sub: What each customer owes, split by how many days the invoices are past due.
cust.note: AI drafts a reminder for each invoice more than 60 days old using your Dunning Levels, and flags customers close to their credit limit.

vend.title: Vendor liabilities aging
vend.sub: What you owe each supplier, split by how many days the invoices are past due.
vend.note: AI suggests which supplier invoices to pay this week from due dates and cash in the bank, and flags China suppliers whose balance is due before the container ships.

fc.title: Asset depreciation forecast
fc.sub: Depreciation expected over the next 12 months, by asset class.
fc.note: AI flags moulds whose planned shots will pass their rated life within the forecast period.

hist.title: Asset history sheet
hist.sub: Every asset from opening value to closing value for the year: additions, depreciation, transfers, retirements.
hist.note: Totals tie to the fixed asset accounts on the balance sheet. AI lists any asset where they do not.

status.title: Asset status report
status.sub: Where every asset is and whether it is active, inactive or retired.
status.note: AI flags active assets with no location update in 12 months — good candidates for the yearly asset count.

trx.title: Asset transaction report
trx.sub: Every posting on assets in a period, with the document behind it.
trx.note: Click any line to open the capitalization, retirement, transfer or depreciation document behind it.
rows: V-007 Delivery truck — to Dubai WH-01

sap.title: Export transactions to SAP Business One
sap.sub: Send documents posted in Southfield to an SAP Business One company, period by period.
sap.note: Useful during the parallel run after go-live, or for a group company still on SAP, so both systems show the same figures. Switch it off once SAP is retired. AI compares totals in both systems after each export.

excel.title: Import from Excel
excel.sub: Upload a sheet of master data. Every row is checked before anything is saved.
excel.note: AI matches your Excel columns to ERP fields, flags duplicates and missing VAT numbers, and lists every error before you confirm.
rows: Ready — 3 rows missing a VAT number

sap.title: Import transactions from SAP Business One
sap.sub: Bring your SAP history across, document type by document type.
sap.note: This is the same move shown on Data Import/Export › SAP B1 migration. Each area is compared with SAP totals before switch-over.

fa.title: Import fixed asset master data from Excel
fa.sub: Upload your asset register: cost, date in use, accumulated depreciation and class.
fa.note: AI checks that each asset has a class and that total accumulated depreciation matches your last balance sheet.

fin.title: Financial template import wizard
fin.sub: Bring in financial report layouts and map their lines to your accounts.
fin.note: AI maps each report line to accounts from your chart of accounts and shows any account that is not used in a report.

act.title: Time sheet activity types
act.sub: The kinds of work staff log hours against on their time sheet.
act.note: Staff fill in time sheets from the Staff Portal on their phone. Hours feed payroll overtime and the cost of service calls; AI flags missing days and unusual overtime before payroll runs.
rows: Travel to a site or factory
QC team in Shenzhen, Foshan, Dongguan, Ningbo

tpl.title: Contract templates
tpl.sub: Ready-made terms for service contracts. A new contract copies its template, then you adjust it.
tpl.note: AI warns 60 days before a contract ends and drafts a renewal quotation from the same template.
rows: No cover — every visit is invoiced

queues.title: Queues
queues.sub: Teams that service calls are assigned to. Anyone in a queue can pick up its calls.
queues.note: AI sends each new service call to the right queue from the customer, item and problem, and moves calls that pass their response time to Escalations.
rows: Claims passed back to China suppliers

fields.title: Bin location field activation
fields.sub: Switch on the levels that make up a bin code (up to 4) and the extra attributes a bin can carry.
fields.note: Once bins hold stock, an active level cannot be switched off — plan the levels before go-live.
rows: A fast movers · B slow movers · Q quarantine

attr.title: Bin location attribute codes
attr.sub: The allowed values for each bin attribute.
attr.note: On goods receipt, AI suggests a bin that fits the carton size and weight, and puts fast movers close to dispatch.

codes.title: Warehouse sublevel codes
codes.sub: The codes for each level. Bin codes are built from them, e.g. WH01-A-03-L2-05.
codes.note: The same codes can be reused in every warehouse, so staff learn one layout.

mgmt.title: Warehouse sublevel code management
mgmt.sub: Create, rename or switch off many sublevel codes at once.
mgmt.note: Before a rename or switch-off, AI shows how many bins and how much stock it touches, and blocks it if stock is still inside.

lc.title: Landed cost codes
lc.sub: Charges added to the cost of imported goods, and how each charge is split across the items in a shipment.
lc.note: When a container arrives, AI matches the forwarder, customs and clearing invoices to the shipment and drafts the landed cost document, so item cost is complete before the goods are sold. Import VAT is not a landed cost: it goes through reverse charge (Setup › Financials › Tax).

atp.title: ATP checking rules
atp.sub: Available-to-promise: what the system counts before it promises a quantity and date on a sales order.
atp.note: Available-to-Promise is switched on in Southfield (it was off in your old SAP Sales module). Sales orders check these rules before a quantity and date are promised, and AI warns a salesperson before they promise stock that is already taken.
rows: On hand + incoming POs − open orders
On hand + goods in transit from China
Items bought through the China offices
On hand in the order’s warehouse
Planned production orders, no stock check

groups.title: Tax groups
groups.sub: One code per VAT treatment. Every document line gets one of these.
groups.note: AI flags any sales line with no tax group, or a 0% code on a customer inside the UAE, before the invoice is posted.

det.title: Tax code determination
det.sub: Picks the tax group automatically. Rules are checked top to bottom; the first match wins.
det.note: Users can still change the tax group on a line, but AI asks for a reason and logs it.

wht.title: Withholding tax
wht.sub: Tax held back from a supplier payment and paid to the government.
wht.note: The UAE does not use withholding tax on normal payments today, so these codes are kept but switched off. Turn one on only if an office outside the UAE needs it.

boxes.title: Tax declaration boxes
boxes.sub: Which tax groups feed each box of the UAE VAT return (VAT 201).
boxes.note: AI fills the VAT return from these boxes each quarter and shows any invoice that does not fit a box before you file.

reports.title: Reports
reports.desc: Same report groups and order as SAP Business One (MRP left out: not used), plus Ask AI for a Report (tagged New).

hr.title: Human Resources
hr.desc: Same 3 functions as SAP Business One first, then 6 new ones (tagged New) for duties, attendance, leave, payroll and the Staff Portal — the staff control SAP was missing.

service.title: Service
service.desc: Same 6 functions, same order as SAP Business One. Warranty claims, service calls and contracts for products in the market.

production.title: Production
production.desc: Same 10 functions, same order as SAP Business One. Bills of materials, production orders and costs for in-house manufacturing.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.desc: Same 10 functions, same order as SAP Business One, including your custom Commitment Master. Stock in Dubai and in transit from China.

banking.title: Banking
banking.desc: Same 9 functions, same order as SAP Business One. Money in and money out — supplier deposits and balances are approved before they leave.

bp.title: Business Partners
bp.desc: Same 7 functions, same order as SAP Business One, including your custom Trademark Master. Every customer and supplier in one place.

purchasing.title: Purchasing
purchasing.desc: Same 22 functions, same order as SAP Business One, including your custom PI tracking, artwork and logistics. From the four China offices to Dubai.

financials.title: Financials
financials.desc: Same 19 functions, same order as SAP Business One. General ledger, VAT and period close for every company in the group.

sales.title: Sales
sales.desc: Same 22 functions, same order as SAP Business One. Quotation to payment, with discount limits and credit checks built in.

AP: Payment to new or changed bank account
Supplier bank details changed in last 30 days
